question:
Two identical setups consist of two smooth vertical conducting rails separated by a distance $l$ and connected at the top by a fixed resistor $R$ (rail resistance negligible). A conducting rod of length $l$ is placed horizontally across the rails and is released from rest so that it slides downward under gravity while maintaining contact. A uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to the plane of the rails.

Setup 1 uses a rod of mass $m_1$ and setup 2 uses a rod of the same dimensions but larger mass $m_2$ (because its material has higher mass density). Assume the external resistance is the same $R$ in both setups, and neglect self-inductance and friction.

Analyze their terminal velocities $v_{T1}$ and $v_{T2}$.

options.A: The rod with higher mass density has a higher terminal velocity.
options.B: The rod with lower mass density has a higher terminal velocity.
options.C: Both rods have the same terminal velocity.
options.D: Terminal velocity is independent of mass.
